stps.description: The Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social (STPS) is the Mexican federal government agency responsible for promoting employment, regulating labor relations, and ensuring decent and safe working conditions for workers.
stps.audit_description: The STPS issues Official Mexican Standards (NOM) on occupational safety and health, conducts labor inspections, and sanctions non-compliance. Its standards are mandatory for all workplaces in Mexico.

imss.description: The Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social (IMSS) is Mexico's largest social security institution, responsible for providing health services, pensions, and social benefits to workers and their families.
imss.audit_description: The IMSS verifies compliance with employer obligations regarding worker registration, payment of employer-employee contributions, and social security benefits. Irregularities may result in tax credits, fines, and surcharges.

infonavit.description: The Instituto del Fondo Nacional de la Vivienda para los Trabajadores (INFONAVIT) manages the workers' housing fund and provides mortgage loans to beneficiaries.
infonavit.audit_description: INFONAVIT audits the correct payment of the 5% employer housing contributions based on workers' integrated salary. Non-compliance generates tax credits and may affect workers' access to their housing rights.

repse.description: The Registro de Prestadoras de Servicios Especializados u Obras Especializadas (REPSE) is the mandatory registry for companies that provide specialized services or execute specialized works through subcontracting.
repse.audit_description: The STPS, through REPSE, verifies that contractor and subcontractor companies are properly registered and that specialized service contracts comply with the subcontracting reform requirements (Decree DOF 23/04/2021).

jfca.description: The Junta Federal de Conciliación y Arbitraje (JFCA) is the federal labor tribunal responsible for resolving individual and collective labor disputes in federally-regulated industries.
jfca.audit_description: The JFCA handles individual and collective labor claims, union disputes, and collective bargaining agreement registrations. Maintaining complete and updated employee records is essential for properly defending the company before this authority.

sat.description: The Servicio de Administración Tributaria (SAT) is the decentralized agency of the Ministry of Finance responsible for collecting and auditing federal taxes in Mexico.
sat.audit_description: The SAT audits compliance with payroll-related tax obligations: income tax on wages, VAT on specialized services, issuance of payroll electronic invoices (CFDI), and proper deduction of labor expenses. Irregularities may result in tax credits, fines, and potential criminal penalties.

inai.description: The Instituto Nacional de Transparencia, Acceso a la Información y Protección de Datos Personales (INAI) is the autonomous body that guarantees the right of access to public information and the protection of personal data.
inai.audit_description: The INAI supervises compliance with the Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (LFPDPPP). Employers must implement a privacy notice for employees, obtain consent for processing sensitive data, and establish adequate security measures.

consar.description: The Comisión Nacional del Sistema de Ahorro para el Retiro (CONSAR) regulates and supervises the Retirement Savings System (SAR), including the AFOREs and SIEFOREs that manage workers' retirement savings.
consar.audit_description: CONSAR verifies the correct payment of SAR contributions (retirement, unemployment, and old-age quotas), both employer and government contributions. Errors in salary records or in the transmission of affiliation movements may reduce workers' retirement account balances.

nom_035_stps_2018.scope: Applies to all workplaces in Mexico. Workplaces with up to 15 workers implement basic measures; those with 16 to 50 workers apply the policy and minimum controls; workplaces with more than 50 workers must comply with all requirements including psychosocial risk factor assessment.
nom_035_stps_2018.audit_description: Mandatory compliance standard establishing elements to identify, analyze, and prevent psychosocial risk factors. The STPS may impose fines of 50 to 5,000 times the UMA (approx. $5,200 to $520,000 MXN) for non-compliance with its provisions.

nom_037_stps_2023.scope: Applies to workplaces with telework arrangements where teleworkers represent 40% or more of the workforce. Employers may opt for its application at lower percentages.
nom_037_stps_2023.audit_description: NOM-037-STPS-2023 establishes occupational safety and health conditions for telework. The STPS may verify compliance through inspections and impose fines of 50 to 5,000 times the UMA for each violation detected.

5.title: Chapter 5 — Employer Obligations
5.obligation: The employer must comply with the obligations established in this chapter to identify, analyze, prevent, and control psychosocial risk factors.
5.explanation: The employer is the primary party responsible for ensuring a favorable organizational environment and implementing all actions required by NOM-035.
5.rationale: Employer obligations are the foundation of the standard; without compliance, it is not possible to protect the mental health of workers.
5.audit_criteria: Verify that the employer has a policy, assessments, action plans, and updated records in accordance with the standard.

5_1.title: 5.1 — Psychosocial Risk Prevention Policy
5_1.obligation: The employer must have a psychosocial risk prevention policy that includes: prevention of psychosocial risk factors, promotion of a favorable organizational environment, and prevention of workplace violence.
5_1.explanation: A policy document signed by management covering all three mandatory elements must be drafted, approved, and disseminated.
5_1.rationale: The policy is the formal declaration of the organization's commitment to occupational mental health.
5_1.audit_criteria: Review the policy document: existence, management signature, date, content of the three elements, and evidence of dissemination.

5_1_1.obligation: The policy must include prevention of psychosocial risk factors.
5_1_1.explanation: Explicitly include in the policy the intention to identify and control psychosocial risk factors.
5_1_1.rationale: Without this explicit declaration, the policy does not meet the minimum requirement of the standard.
5_1_1.audit_criteria: Confirm that the policy text mentions the prevention of psychosocial risk factors.

5_1_2.obligation: The policy must promote a favorable organizational environment.
5_1_2.explanation: The document must commit to creating working conditions that foster well-being and mental health.
5_1_2.rationale: A favorable organizational environment is the central objective of NOM-035.
5_1_2.audit_criteria: Verify that the policy declares commitment to promoting a favorable organizational environment.

5_1_3.obligation: The policy must include prevention of workplace violence.
5_1_3.explanation: Expressly declare the commitment to prevent, address, and sanction any act of workplace violence.
5_1_3.rationale: Workplace violence is one of the most serious psychosocial risk factors and has direct legal consequences.
5_1_3.audit_criteria: Confirm that the policy addresses prevention of workplace violence with defined response mechanisms.

5_2.title: 5.2 — Identification and Analysis of Psychosocial Risk Factors
5_2.obligation: The employer must identify and analyze psychosocial risk factors using the standard's reference guides or equivalent validated instruments.
5_2.explanation: Apply the questionnaire or reference guide to all workers to detect conditions that generate psychosocial risk.
5_2.rationale: Without identification, it is not possible to implement effective controls; this step is the standard's diagnostic phase.
5_2.audit_criteria: Request the assessment instrument applied, the population of evaluated workers, the date, and the results obtained.

5_2_1.obligation: The identification must cover all psychosocial risk factors defined in the standard: work environment conditions, workloads, lack of control over work, working hours exceeding those provided in the LFT, work-family interference, negative leadership, negative workplace relationships, and workplace violence.
5_2_1.explanation: The applied instrument must cover all psychosocial risk domains listed in NOM-035 without exception.
5_2_1.rationale: Omitting any factor invalidates the assessment and leaves real risk areas for workers without coverage.
5_2_1.audit_criteria: Review that the instrument and results report contain analysis of all factors listed in the standard.

5_2_2.obligation: When the identification reveals psychosocial risk factors, the employer must conduct analysis to determine the necessary control measures.
5_2_2.explanation: The diagnostic results must be processed to prioritize controls according to the level of risk identified.
5_2_2.rationale: Analysis converts raw data into actionable information to protect workers' health.
5_2_2.audit_criteria: Verify that an analysis report exists following the assessment, with risk prioritization and proposed controls.

5_3.title: 5.3 — Adoption of Prevention and Control Measures
5_3.obligation: The employer must adopt the necessary measures to prevent and control the identified psychosocial risk factors.
5_3.explanation: Based on the analysis, implement concrete actions to eliminate or reduce the identified risk factors.
5_3.rationale: Control implementation is the core of the standard; diagnosis without action does not achieve the objective of protecting health.
5_3.audit_criteria: Request the action plan with measures, responsible parties, dates, and evidence of implementation.

5_3_1.obligation: Measures must aim to eliminate or reduce the identified psychosocial risk factors.
5_3_1.explanation: Prioritize elimination of the risk source; when not possible, reduce its intensity or duration.
5_3_1.rationale: The hierarchy of controls requires acting on the source before resorting to administrative controls or PPE.
5_3_1.audit_criteria: Verify that the action plan measures directly correspond to the risk factors identified in the assessment.

5_3_2.obligation: Measures must promote a favorable organizational environment.
5_3_2.explanation: In addition to eliminating risks, implement proactive actions that improve the organizational climate and worker well-being.
5_3_2.rationale: The standard's approach is dual: eliminate the negative and strengthen the positive in the work environment.
5_3_2.audit_criteria: Confirm that the plan includes organizational environment improvement actions, not just reactive controls.

5_4.title: 5.4 — Policy and Results Dissemination
5_4.obligation: The employer must disseminate the psychosocial risk prevention policy to workers and inform them of the identification and analysis results.
5_4.explanation: Formally communicate the current policy and diagnostic findings to all workers.
5_4.rationale: Informed worker participation is a requirement of the standard and a key success factor of the program.
5_4.audit_criteria: Review dissemination records: attendance lists, communication records, or visible posting in the facility.

5_4_1.obligation: Disseminate the psychosocial risk prevention policy to all workers at the workplace.
5_4_1.explanation: Ensure 100% of workers know the policy, using communication methods appropriate for the workplace.
5_4_1.rationale: A policy that workers are unaware of does not generate the cultural change the standard pursues.
5_4_1.audit_criteria: Request evidence of dissemination with dates and coverage: publications, emails, meetings, or posters.

5_4_2.obligation: Inform workers of the results of the identification and analysis of psychosocial risk factors.
5_4_2.explanation: Communicate the diagnostic results in an understandable manner without compromising individual confidentiality.
5_4_2.rationale: Transparency builds trust and motivates active worker participation in solutions.
5_4_2.audit_criteria: Verify that workers received communication about the general results of the assessment.

5_5.title: 5.5 — Promote a Favorable Organizational Environment
5_5.obligation: The employer must actively promote a favorable organizational environment through actions that foster respectful treatment, teamwork, training, and recognition.
5_5.explanation: Implement programs and practices that strengthen protective factors in the work environment.
5_5.rationale: A favorable organizational environment reduces the incidence of stress, burnout, and workplace violence.
5_5.audit_criteria: Review evidence of environment improvement actions: wellness programs, training, recognition initiatives, and climate surveys.

5_6.title: 5.6 — Support for Workers Exposed to Workplace Violence
5_6.obligation: The employer must provide mechanisms to support workers who have been subjected to workplace violence or who show symptoms associated with psychosocial risk factors.
5_6.explanation: Establish reporting channels, response protocols, and referral to health services when necessary.
5_6.rationale: Timely support reduces health damage and the employer's legal liability.
5_6.audit_criteria: Verify the existence of response protocols, records of cases handled, and follow-up mechanisms.

5_7.title: 5.7 — Medical Examinations
5_7.obligation: The employer must conduct medical examinations and psychological evaluations for personnel exposed to psychosocial risk factors, in accordance with NOM-030-STPS-2009.
5_7.explanation: Conduct specific examinations at the indicated frequency to detect health damage resulting from exposure to psychosocial risks.
5_7.rationale: Medical surveillance enables early detection of health effects and allows preventive action before they escalate.
5_7.audit_criteria: Request records of medical examinations and psychological evaluations conducted, including dates and coverage of exposed personnel.

5_8.title: 5.8 — Records and Information Retention
5_8.obligation: The employer must maintain records on the identification and analysis of psychosocial risk factors, measures adopted, and evaluation results, retaining them for at least 4 years.
5_8.explanation: Maintain updated files with all documentation generated during implementation of the standard for the minimum required period.
5_8.rationale: Records are the evidence of compliance during a STPS inspection and demonstrate the program's traceability.
5_8.audit_criteria: Request records of assessments, action plans, medical examinations, and any documentation generated in implementing the standard.

5_8_a.obligation: Retain records of the identification and analysis of psychosocial risk factors for at least 4 years.
5_8_a.explanation: Archive the applied instruments, raw results, and analysis reports from each assessment cycle.
5_8_a.rationale: 4-year retention allows trend comparison between cycles and demonstrates program continuity to the authority.
5_8_a.audit_criteria: Verify that identification and analysis records are available for the last 4 years of operation.

5_8_b.obligation: Retain records of measures adopted to prevent and control psychosocial risk factors for at least 4 years.
5_8_b.explanation: Document and archive all action plans, their progress, modifications, and results obtained.
5_8_b.rationale: The history of implemented actions is evidence of continuous improvement effort and proactive compliance.
5_8_b.audit_criteria: Request action plans from the last 4 years with implementation dates and follow-up evidence.

5_8_c.obligation: Retain records of medical examinations and psychological evaluations conducted for at least 4 years.
5_8_c.explanation: Maintain individual medical records and psychological evaluation results under confidential custody during the minimum required period.
5_8_c.rationale: Medical records are evidence of health surveillance and compliance with the standard's obligations.
5_8_c.audit_criteria: Verify that medical records and psychological evaluations from the last 4 years are available and under adequate custody.

8.title: Chapter 8 — Conformity Assessment
8.obligation: This chapter establishes the procedures for verifying compliance with NOM-035-STPS-2018 by competent authorities.
8.explanation: Defines how the STPS and its inspectors assess whether a workplace complies with the standard's provisions.
8.rationale: Conformity assessment is the enforcement mechanism that ensures the effectiveness of the standard.
8.audit_criteria: Understand the verification procedure to prepare documentation and facilitate inspections.

8_1.title: 8.1 — Verification at Workplaces
8_1.obligation: Verification of the standard's compliance at workplaces will be conducted in accordance with procedures established in NOM-019-STPS-2011 and other applicable legal provisions.
8_1.explanation: STPS inspections will follow the defined protocol, with prior notice or unannounced depending on the law.
8_1.rationale: Understanding the verification process allows proper preparation of the required documentary evidence.
8_1.audit_criteria: Keep all standard documentation current, accessible, and organized to facilitate any inspection.

8_1_1.obligation: The inspector will review the existence and content of the psychosocial risk prevention policy.
8_1_1.explanation: During the inspection, the inspector will request the policy document and evaluate whether it meets the requirements of clause 5.1.
8_1_1.rationale: The policy is the first element verified as it is the formal declaration of the employer's commitment.
8_1_1.audit_criteria: Have the signed policy document available with date and evidence of dissemination to workers.

8_1_2.obligation: The inspector will review records of identification and analysis of psychosocial risk factors.
8_1_2.explanation: Applied assessment instruments, results obtained, and corresponding analysis will be requested.
8_1_2.rationale: Assessment records are the central evidence of technical compliance with the standard.
8_1_2.audit_criteria: Prepare a file with the assessment instrument, individual and consolidated results, and the analysis report.

8_1_3.obligation: The inspector will review the action plan to prevent and control identified psychosocial risk factors.
8_1_3.explanation: The action plan with adopted measures, responsible parties, dates, and implementation progress will be reviewed.
8_1_3.rationale: The action plan demonstrates that assessment results were translated into concrete measures.
8_1_3.audit_criteria: Have a formal action plan with dates, responsible parties, progress indicators, and implementation evidence.

8_1_4.obligation: The inspector will review records of medical examinations and psychological evaluations conducted on exposed workers.
8_1_4.explanation: Medical records and psychological evaluations with their respective dates and coverage will be requested.
8_1_4.rationale: Medical surveillance is evidence that the employer monitors the impact of risks on workers' health.
8_1_4.audit_criteria: Have medical records and psychological evaluations from the last 4 years available, under confidential custody.

8_2.title: 8.2 — Verification Criteria for Workplaces with Up to 15 Workers
8_2.obligation: Workplaces with up to 15 workers will be verified according to the simplified criteria established in this clause.
8_2.explanation: Smaller workplaces have reduced requirements: basic policy, dissemination of control measures, and minimum records.
8_2.rationale: The standard recognizes that small workplaces have limited capacity and resources to implement complex programs.
8_2.audit_criteria: For workplaces with up to 15 workers, verify: policy, basic control measures, and record of actions taken.

8_2_1.obligation: For workplaces with up to 15 workers: have the psychosocial risk prevention policy (5.1).
8_2_1.explanation: Even in the smallest workplaces, the policy is mandatory and must be documented and disseminated.
8_2_1.rationale: The policy is the universal minimum requirement of the standard, regardless of workplace size.
8_2_1.audit_criteria: Review the existence of the policy document and evidence that it was communicated to workers.

8_2_2.obligation: For workplaces with up to 15 workers: disseminate the adopted control measures to workers.
8_2_2.explanation: Communicate to workers the actions implemented to control identified psychosocial risks.
8_2_2.rationale: Worker participation in the program depends on their awareness of the measures adopted.
8_2_2.audit_criteria: Request evidence of dissemination: communication records, attendance lists, or internal publications.

8_2_3.obligation: For workplaces with up to 15 workers: keep records of prevention and control actions taken.
8_2_3.explanation: Document, even in a simple format, the actions implemented to prevent and control risks.
8_2_3.rationale: Records, even basic ones, are evidence of compliance effort during an inspection.
8_2_3.audit_criteria: Review that records of actions taken exist with dates and description of implemented measures.

8_2_4.obligation: For workplaces with up to 15 workers: provide support to workers who show symptoms associated with psychosocial risk factors.
8_2_4.explanation: Have a basic mechanism for workers to report risk situations and receive attention.
8_2_4.rationale: Timely support reduces health damage and is a basic requirement of the standard for all workplace sizes.
8_2_4.audit_criteria: Verify that a reporting and support mechanism exists and that workers are aware of it.

8_3.title: 8.3 — Verification Criteria for Workplaces with 16 to 50 Workers
8_3.obligation: Workplaces with 16 to 50 workers will be verified according to the Phase 1 implementation criteria established in this clause.
8_3.explanation: These workplaces must comply with the policy, basic control measures, and records, without the obligation of full Reference Guide III assessment.
8_3.rationale: Phase 1 introduces progressive requirements for mid-size workplaces, recognizing their greater operational capacity.
8_3.audit_criteria: For workplaces with 16-50 workers, verify: policy, basic factor identification, control measures, and records of actions.

8_3_1.obligation: For workplaces with 16 to 50 workers: have the psychosocial risk prevention policy and have disseminated it.
8_3_1.explanation: The policy must be documented, approved by management, and disseminated to all workplace workers.
8_3_1.rationale: The formal policy is the starting point for any psychosocial risk management program.
8_3_1.audit_criteria: Request the policy document with management signature and evidence of dissemination to all workers.

8_3_2.obligation: For workplaces with 16 to 50 workers: have identified psychosocial risk factors using the corresponding reference guide.
8_3_2.explanation: Apply Reference Guide II or another equivalent instrument to identify risk factors in the workplace.
8_3_2.rationale: Formal risk identification is the key technical requirement that distinguishes Phase 1 from the basic level.
8_3_2.audit_criteria: Request the applied instrument, application date, worker coverage, and results obtained.

8_3_3.obligation: For workplaces with 16 to 50 workers: have adopted control measures for the identified risk factors.
8_3_3.explanation: Based on identification results, implement concrete prevention and control actions.
8_3_3.rationale: Control implementation closes the standard's cycle and is the indicator of effective compliance.
8_3_3.audit_criteria: Review the action plan with specific measures corresponding to the identified risk factors.

8_3_4.obligation: For workplaces with 16 to 50 workers: keep records of risk factor identification and adopted control measures.
8_3_4.explanation: Document and archive assessment results and implemented actions during the minimum required period.
8_3_4.rationale: Records are the primary evidence of compliance during a STPS inspection.
8_3_4.audit_criteria: Verify the existence and completeness of records during the minimum 4-year retention period.

8_4.title: 8.4 — Verification Criteria for Workplaces with More Than 50 Workers
8_4.obligation: Workplaces with more than 50 workers will be verified according to the full Phase 2 implementation criteria.
8_4.explanation: These workplaces must comply with all standard requirements: policy, full assessment with Reference Guide III, action plan, control measures, follow-up, and medical examinations.
8_4.rationale: Large workplaces have greater resource capacity and their scale amplifies the impact of psychosocial risks.
8_4.audit_criteria: Verify full compliance: policy, Reference Guide III assessment, analysis, action plan, medical examinations, and complete records.

8_4_1.obligation: For workplaces with more than 50 workers: have the policy, have disseminated it, and review it periodically.
8_4_1.explanation: The policy must be reviewed at least once a year and updated when working conditions change.
8_4_1.rationale: Periodic review ensures the policy reflects the current reality of the workplace.
8_4_1.audit_criteria: Request the policy revision history and evidence of dissemination of the current version.

8_4_2.obligation: For workplaces with more than 50 workers: have assessed psychosocial risk factors using Reference Guide III or an equivalent instrument.
8_4_2.explanation: Apply the full assessment to all workers and process results using the established methodology.
8_4_2.rationale: Full assessment with Guide III provides a detailed and statistically valid diagnosis.
8_4_2.audit_criteria: Review that the assessment was applied to all workers, with results analyzed by area or department.

8_4_3.obligation: For workplaces with more than 50 workers: have adopted control measures, monitor their effectiveness, and maintain records.
8_4_3.explanation: Implement action plan measures, monitor their impact, and document follow-up results.
8_4_3.rationale: Follow-up closes the continuous improvement cycle and demonstrates that implemented measures are effective.
8_4_3.audit_criteria: Request the action plan with indicators, review dates, follow-up results, and adjustments made.

8_4_4.obligation: For workplaces with more than 50 workers: conduct medical examinations and psychological evaluations for exposed personnel and maintain corresponding records.
8_4_4.explanation: Conduct entry, periodic, and exit examinations for personnel exposed to psychosocial risk factors.
8_4_4.rationale: Continuous medical surveillance is the most precise indicator of the real impact of psychosocial risks on workers' health.
8_4_4.audit_criteria: Verify that examinations are conducted for all exposed personnel at the indicated frequency and that records are current.

8_5.title: 8.5 — Verification Units
8_5.obligation: Conformity assessment of NOM-035-STPS-2018 may be carried out by verification units accredited by EMA or directly by the STPS through its inspectors.
8_5.explanation: Workplaces may hire an accredited verification unit to obtain a voluntary compliance certificate.
8_5.rationale: Third-party accredited verification offers greater objectivity and may be useful for clients or investors requiring compliance evidence.
8_5.audit_criteria: If a verification unit was hired, request the issued report and certificate; verify the validity of the accreditation.

8_5_1.obligation: Verification units must be accredited by the Mexican Accreditation Entity (EMA) for NOM-035-STPS-2018.
8_5_1.explanation: Before hiring a verification unit, confirm it is specifically accredited for NOM-035 at EMA.
8_5_1.rationale: Only EMA-accredited units can issue compliance certificates with official validity.
8_5_1.audit_criteria: Verify the verification unit's accreditation number in EMA's public directory.

8_5_2.obligation: The verification unit must review workplace documentation according to the applicable verification criteria based on workplace size.
8_5_2.explanation: Document review is the first stage of verification and determines whether the workplace meets its category's requirements.
8_5_2.rationale: Systematic document review ensures no requirements are omitted in the evaluation process.
8_5_2.audit_criteria: The verification unit's report must indicate which documents were reviewed and which show conformity or non-conformity.

8_5_3.obligation: The verification unit must visit the workplace to verify working conditions on-site.
8_5_3.explanation: The on-site visit complements document review and allows verification of actual physical and organizational conditions.
8_5_3.rationale: On-site verification detects situations that are not documented but represent real risks to workers.
8_5_3.audit_criteria: The report must include on-site visit findings with description of observed conditions.

8_5_4.obligation: The verification unit must issue a conformity or non-conformity opinion regarding NOM-035-STPS-2018 provisions.
8_5_4.explanation: Upon completing verification, the unit issues a formal opinion indicating the workplace's degree of compliance.
8_5_4.rationale: The formal opinion is the document certifying the verification result and may be presented to clients, authorities, or partners.
8_5_4.audit_criteria: Request the opinion issued by the verification unit with date, scope, findings, and conformity resolution.

5.title: Chapter 5 — Employer Obligations
5.obligation: The employer must comply with the obligations established in this chapter to guarantee safety and health conditions in the telework modality.
5.explanation: The employer is the primary party responsible for ensuring that telework conditions are safe, ergonomic, and respectful of workers' rights.
5.rationale: Employer obligations in telework are the foundation of NOM-037; without compliance, it is not possible to guarantee the physical and mental integrity of the teleworker.
5.audit_criteria: Verify that the employer has a policy, equipment, telework agreements, records, and evidence of training in accordance with the standard.

5_1.title: 5.1 — Safety and Health Conditions at the Telework Location
5_1.obligation: The employer must verify that the telework location designated by the worker has adequate safety and health conditions, in accordance with the minimum requirements established in the standard.
5_1.explanation: Before authorizing telework, the employer must confirm that the domestic or external space used by the worker meets minimum safety, lighting, ventilation, and ergonomic conditions.
5_1.rationale: The employer retains the obligation to protect the safety and health of the worker even when the activity is performed outside the workplace.
5_1.audit_criteria: Request the telework location verification mechanism (checklist, virtual visit, worker declaration) and records of verifications performed.

5_1_I.obligation: Verify that the telework location has adequate natural or artificial lighting conditions for performing activities.
5_1_I.explanation: The space must have sufficient light to avoid visual fatigue; this can be validated through a guided self-assessment or virtual visit.
5_1_I.rationale: Inadequate lighting is one of the main causes of eye fatigue and musculoskeletal disorders in office work.
5_1_I.audit_criteria: Verify that the location validation process includes lighting criteria and that records of the evaluation exist.

5_1_II.obligation: Verify that the telework location has adequate ventilation and hygiene conditions.
5_1_II.explanation: The space must allow sufficient air renewal and hygiene conditions that do not pose a health risk to the teleworker.
5_1_II.rationale: Poor environmental conditions can affect the respiratory health and general well-being of the teleworker.
5_1_II.audit_criteria: Confirm that the validation protocol includes ventilation and hygiene criteria for the workspace.

5_1_III.obligation: Verify that the telework location has electrical installations in safe condition.
5_1_III.explanation: The electrical installations of the telework space must not pose a risk of short circuit, overload, or accidental electrical contact.
5_1_III.rationale: Electrical deficiencies are a frequent cause of accidents in the home and can cause everything from burns to fires.
5_1_III.audit_criteria: Include verification of electrical installations in the telework space validation protocol.

5_1_IV.obligation: Verify that the telework location has adequate furniture and ergonomic conditions.
5_1_IV.explanation: The chair, desk, and equipment arrangement must allow a correct posture that prevents musculoskeletal disorders.
5_1_IV.rationale: Prolonged work in an inadequate posture is one of the main causes of occupational illness in telework.
5_1_IV.audit_criteria: Review that ergonomic conditions of furniture are evaluated and that records of the evaluation exist.

5_1_V.obligation: Verify that the telework location has adequate internet or telecommunications connectivity for performing activities.
5_1_V.explanation: Connectivity must be sufficient for the required digital work tools, without interruptions that generate additional workload.
5_1_V.rationale: Poor connectivity generates stress, affects productivity, and can translate into extended working hours.
5_1_V.audit_criteria: Confirm that the validation process includes connectivity criteria and that the employer supports workers in resolving connectivity issues.

5_1_VI.obligation: Verify that the telework location is free from risk conditions that could cause occupational accidents.
5_1_VI.explanation: The space must not have obstacles, slippery surfaces, exposed cables, or other conditions that pose a risk of falling or injury.
5_1_VI.rationale: Accidents at the telework location are considered occupational accidents and generate employer liability.
5_1_VI.audit_criteria: Confirm that the validation protocol includes a visual walkthrough or general risk conditions checklist.

5_2.title: 5.2 — Work Equipment and Tools
5_2.obligation: The employer must provide, install, and maintain in good condition the work equipment and tools necessary for telework performance.
5_2.explanation: The employer is responsible for providing the necessary technological equipment (computer, phone, software) and keeping it functional.
5_2.rationale: The teleworker must not bear the cost or responsibility for work equipment; this obligation falls on the employer.
5_2.audit_criteria: Request the inventory of equipment assigned to teleworkers, loan agreements or custody documents, and maintenance records.

5_2_I.obligation: Provide the teleworker with the computing, telecommunications, and other technological tools necessary for performing their activities.
5_2_I.explanation: Before starting telework, the employer must deliver or guarantee access to the necessary equipment, with documented custody.
5_2_I.rationale: Workers cannot be held responsible for acquiring work equipment; the standard is clear that this is an employer obligation.
5_2_I.audit_criteria: Review loan agreements, equipment delivery-reception records, or any document certifying the provision of equipment.

5_2_II.obligation: Install and maintain in safe and good condition the equipment and tools provided to the teleworker.
5_2_II.explanation: The employer must ensure that equipment reaches the worker in operational condition and that a preventive and corrective maintenance process exists.
5_2_II.rationale: Defective equipment generates interruptions, stress, and IT security risks that negatively impact the teleworker.
5_2_II.audit_criteria: Request maintenance records for equipment assigned to teleworkers and response times for reported failures.

5_2_III.obligation: Assume the costs derived from telework, including the payment of telecommunications services and the proportional share of electricity.
5_2_III.explanation: The employer must cover the additional internet and electricity expenses incurred by the worker due to telework, as agreed.
5_2_III.rationale: Telework costs must not be transferred to the worker; the standard defines these as an employer obligation.
5_2_III.audit_criteria: Verify that a documented mechanism exists for reimbursement or payment of telecommunications and energy services to the teleworker.

5_2_IV.obligation: Keep a record of the equipment and tools provided to each teleworker.
5_2_IV.explanation: Maintain an updated inventory of assets assigned in telework modality, with worker data, equipment description, and dates.
5_2_IV.rationale: The record enables equipment traceability, facilitates recovery at the end of the modality, and certifies compliance to the authority.
5_2_IV.audit_criteria: Request the record or inventory of equipment assigned to teleworkers; verify that it is up to date.

5_3.title: 5.3 — Ergonomics
5_3.obligation: The employer must provide information, training, and guidance to the teleworker on ergonomics, in order to prevent musculoskeletal disorders and visual fatigue.
5_3.explanation: Instruct the worker on the correct configuration of their workstation, posture, and active breaks to prevent injuries.
5_3.rationale: Poor ergonomics is the main cause of occupational diseases in office work; its prevention requires specific training.
5_3.audit_criteria: Request the ergonomics training program or materials and records of workers who received it.

5_3_I.obligation: Provide the teleworker with information on ergonomic risks associated with telework and applicable prevention measures.
5_3_I.explanation: Deliver guides, manuals, or infographics with criteria for workstation configuration, correct posture, and warning signs of musculoskeletal disorders.
5_3_I.rationale: A worker who understands ergonomic risks can take preventive measures autonomously in their workspace.
5_3_I.audit_criteria: Review the informational materials delivered and the worker's receipt records.

5_3_II.obligation: Train the teleworker in the correct configuration of their workstation to minimize ergonomic risks.
5_3_II.explanation: Include in the training program criteria for monitor height, keyboard position, lumbar support, and visual distance.
5_3_II.rationale: Incorrect workstation configuration is correctable with training; training is the most cost-effective preventive measure.
5_3_II.audit_criteria: Request the content of the ergonomic training and the attendance records or certificates of teleworkers.

5_3_III.obligation: Promote the practice of active breaks and stretching exercises during the telework workday.
5_3_III.explanation: Implement mechanisms that remind teleworkers to take brief breaks and stretches to counteract the effects of prolonged posture.
5_3_III.rationale: Active breaks reduce muscle tension, improve circulation, and contribute to the general well-being of the teleworker.
5_3_III.audit_criteria: Verify that a formal active breaks program exists and that teleworkers are informed of its implementation.

5_4.title: 5.4 — Training and Development
5_4.obligation: The employer must provide training to the teleworker on the safe use of information technologies, prevention of occupational risks in telework, and the rights and obligations derived from the standard.
5_4.explanation: Design and deliver a specific training program for telework covering technological tools, information security, ergonomics, and NOM-037 provisions.
5_4.rationale: Adequate training is a necessary condition for telework to be safe, productive, and legally compliant.
5_4.audit_criteria: Request the training program for teleworkers, attendance certificates, and evidence that it covers the topics required by the standard.

5_4_I.obligation: Train the teleworker in the adequate and safe use of the equipment and work tools provided.
5_4_I.explanation: Instruct the worker in the correct handling of the assigned equipment, including basic IT security measures.
5_4_I.rationale: Lack of knowledge in equipment use can lead to security incidents or hardware damage that affect operations.
5_4_I.audit_criteria: Review equipment use training certificates for teleworkers.

5_4_II.obligation: Train the teleworker on the occupational risks specific to the telework modality and the applicable prevention measures.
5_4_II.explanation: Include in the training the ergonomic, isolation, workplace violence, and psychosocial risks associated with telework.
5_4_II.rationale: A teleworker exposed to unknown risks cannot protect themselves; preventive training is the employer's obligation.
5_4_II.audit_criteria: Verify that the training covers the specific risks of telework and includes the corresponding prevention measures.

5_4_III.obligation: Inform the teleworker of their rights and obligations under NOM-037-STPS-2023 and other applicable labor provisions.
5_4_III.explanation: Communicate in an accessible manner the teleworker's rights (right to disconnect, privacy, reversibility) and their obligations.
5_4_III.rationale: An informed worker can exercise their rights; an informed worker can fulfill their obligations.
5_4_III.audit_criteria: Review whether informational material on teleworker rights and obligations exists and delivery records.

5_4_IV.obligation: Keep training and development programs up to date in accordance with technological, regulatory, and working conditions changes.
5_4_IV.explanation: Periodically review and update training content to reflect changes in tools, processes, and applicable regulations.
5_4_IV.rationale: Obsolete training programs create knowledge gaps that can lead to unaddressed risks.
5_4_IV.audit_criteria: Verify the date of the last training program update and its correspondence with organizational changes.

5_5.title: 5.5 — Risk Factors Specific to Telework
5_5.obligation: The employer must identify, assess, and control the risk factors specific to the telework modality, including social isolation, work-family interference, and excessive workload.
5_5.explanation: Implement mechanisms for detecting and addressing the specific risks of telework that do not exist or are different in on-site work.
5_5.rationale: Telework introduces specific risks — isolation, hyperconnectivity, difficulty disconnecting — that require active management.
5_5.audit_criteria: Request the telework risk analysis, control plan, and follow-up records.

5_5_I.obligation: Identify and control the risks of social isolation that teleworkers may experience.
5_5_I.explanation: Implement communication and social contact mechanisms that prevent isolation, such as virtual meetings, exchange spaces, and periodic visits to the workplace.
5_5_I.rationale: Social isolation is a psychosocial risk of telework that can lead to anxiety, depression, and reduced work engagement.
5_5_I.audit_criteria: Review the mechanisms implemented to foster social integration of teleworkers.

5_5_II.obligation: Implement mechanisms to prevent interference between work and the personal and family life of the teleworker.
5_5_II.explanation: Establish disconnection policies, clear schedules, and communication channels that respect rest and family time.
5_5_II.rationale: Work-family interference is one of the most frequent risk factors in telework and affects both worker health and productivity.
5_5_II.audit_criteria: Verify that a digital disconnection policy exists and mechanisms to ensure it is respected.

5_5_III.obligation: Control the teleworker's workload to avoid excessive working hours and guarantee respect for rest times established in the LFT.
5_5_III.explanation: Monitor the workload assigned to teleworkers and adjust it to avoid systematic overtime or work outside working hours.
5_5_III.rationale: The invisibility of the teleworker can allow workload to expand beyond legal limits without timely detection.
5_5_III.audit_criteria: Review workday control mechanisms for teleworkers and verify that rest times are respected.

5_6.title: 5.6 — Telework Agreement
5_6.obligation: The employer must enter into a telework agreement with the worker covering the conditions, obligations, and rights of both parties in accordance with the standard.
5_6.explanation: Formalize in writing the telework conditions: location, schedule, equipment, costs, right to disconnect, and reversibility.
5_6.rationale: The agreement formalizes the conditions of telework and protects both the worker and the employer from potential disputes.
5_6.audit_criteria: Request the signed telework agreements and verify that they contain all elements required by the standard.

5_6_I.obligation: The telework agreement must specify the location or locations from which the worker will perform their activities in telework modality.
5_6_I.explanation: Document in the agreement the address or description of the space from which the worker will perform their functions.
5_6_I.rationale: Defining the telework location is essential for the employer to be able to verify safety and health conditions.
5_6_I.audit_criteria: Review that the agreement includes the authorized telework location and any procedure for location changes.

5_6_II.obligation: The telework agreement must establish the work schedule, supervision mechanisms, and the worker's right to disconnect.
5_6_II.explanation: Specify in the agreement the ordinary schedule, channels and frequency of contact, and the hours when the worker will not be required to respond to communications.
5_6_II.rationale: Without a clear agreement on schedules and disconnection, the teleworker is exposed to permanent availability that violates their rights.
5_6_II.audit_criteria: Confirm that the agreement includes schedule, supervision mechanisms, and explicit provisions on the right to disconnect.

5_6_III.obligation: The telework agreement must contemplate the conditions for reversibility, the equipment provided, and the costs assumed by the employer.
5_6_III.explanation: Document the process for returning to on-site work, the inventory of equipment delivered, and the cost reimbursement mechanism.
5_6_III.rationale: Reversibility and the management of equipment and costs, if not agreed upon, generate conflicts at the end of the modality.
5_6_III.audit_criteria: Verify that the agreement includes reversibility clauses, equipment description, and the cost compensation mechanism.

5_7.title: 5.7 — Telework Records and Control
5_7.obligation: The employer must keep an updated record of teleworkers and the conditions under which the service is provided, including the agreements made and the safety condition verifications performed.
5_7.explanation: Maintain a file per teleworker with the signed agreement, the result of the workplace verification, and training and equipment records.
5_7.rationale: Records are evidence of compliance during a STPS inspection and facilitate the management and monitoring of the telework program.
5_7.audit_criteria: Request the teleworker record and individual files; verify that they are complete and up to date.

5_7_I.obligation: Keep an updated record of all workers performing in telework modality, including their data, telework location, and start date.
5_7_I.explanation: Maintain a teleworker registry with basic information that allows identifying the universe of workers subject to the standard.
5_7_I.rationale: The record is the starting point for managing any obligation under the standard; without it, it is not possible to demonstrate the scope of application.
5_7_I.audit_criteria: Verify that the record exists, is up to date, and contains the minimum required data for all teleworkers.

5_7_II.obligation: Retain telework agreements and records of safety and health condition verifications at the telework location.
5_7_II.explanation: Archive signed agreements and evidence of each teleworker's workspace verification for the duration of the modality.
5_7_II.rationale: Document retention certifies compliance before any labor authority or in the event of an occupational accident.
5_7_II.audit_criteria: Request archived agreements and verifications; review that they are available and correspond to active teleworkers.

5_7_III.obligation: Keep records of training delivered to teleworkers in accordance with the standard's requirements.
5_7_III.explanation: Document the training sessions conducted, topics covered, and workers who received them, with corresponding dates.
5_7_III.rationale: Training records are evidence that the employer has fulfilled their training obligations under NOM-037.
5_7_III.audit_criteria: Request attendance lists, training certificates, or any record certifying the training of teleworkers.

5_8.title: 5.8 — Telework Reversibility
5_8.obligation: The employer must guarantee the worker's right to revert to on-site work and return to in-person work, in accordance with the agreements established and the provisions of the Federal Labor Law.
5_8.explanation: When the worker requests a return to on-site work, the employer must facilitate the transition within the agreed timeframe.
5_8.rationale: Reversibility is a fundamental right of the teleworker recognized in the LFT; its violation generates labor liability.
5_8.audit_criteria: Verify that the telework agreement contemplates the reversibility process and that documented cases of return to on-site work exist when requested.

5_8_I.obligation: Agree with the worker on the timeframe and conditions for reverting to the on-site modality when requested.
5_8_I.explanation: The return process must be documented in the telework agreement, with reasonable timeframes and clear conditions.
5_8_I.rationale: Without a formal reversibility process, the worker may face practical obstacles that limit the exercise of their right.
5_8_I.audit_criteria: Review that the agreement establishes the reversibility process and timeframe, and that it has been respected in cases where requested.

5_8_II.obligation: Guarantee that the worker who reverts to the on-site modality retains the same rights and working conditions they had before adopting telework.
5_8_II.explanation: The return to on-site work must not imply loss of salary, category, benefits, or acquired labor rights.
5_8_II.rationale: The inviolability of rights is a labor principle protected by the LFT; any harm to the worker for reverting telework is illegal.
5_8_II.audit_criteria: Verify that in reversion cases, the worker's working conditions were maintained without prejudicial modifications.

5_8_III.obligation: Facilitate the return of equipment and tools when reverting from telework modality, and document the delivery-reception process.
5_8_III.explanation: When telework ends, formalize the return of all assigned equipment through a formal record or equivalent document.
5_8_III.rationale: Documentation of the return protects the employer from equipment claims and the worker from undue liability.
5_8_III.audit_criteria: Request equipment return records in cases of reversion to on-site work.

5_9.title: 5.9 — Gender Perspective and Non-Discrimination
5_9.obligation: The employer must ensure that the implementation of telework does not generate discrimination or reproduce gender stereotypes, ensuring equal conditions for women and men.
5_9.explanation: Telework policies and practices must be designed with a gender perspective to prevent the modality from disproportionately affecting women or reproducing caregiving roles.
5_9.rationale: Telework can reinforce gender inequalities if not managed with an equity perspective; the standard requires active management of this risk.
5_9.audit_criteria: Review whether the telework policy includes a gender perspective and whether the employer monitors the equitable distribution of the modality between men and women.

5_9_I.obligation: Ensure that telework policies promote equal treatment and opportunities for male and female workers.
5_9_I.explanation: The conditions, access criteria, training, and benefits of telework must be applied equally without gender distinction.
5_9_I.rationale: A telework policy without a gender perspective can become an unintentional labor segregation mechanism.
5_9_I.audit_criteria: Verify that the telework policy establishes objective and non-discriminatory criteria for access to and conditions of the modality.

5_9_II.obligation: Prevent telework from generating a greater unpaid domestic workload for female workers.
5_9_II.explanation: Implement mechanisms that clearly separate paid work time from household responsibilities during the workday.
5_9_II.rationale: Female teleworkers frequently face double presence (work and caregiving) that the standard explicitly seeks to prevent.
5_9_II.audit_criteria: Review whether concrete measures exist to prevent double presence and how their effectiveness is verified.

5_9_III.obligation: Ensure that telework is not used as a mechanism to exclude or marginalize female workers from professional development and decision-making processes.
5_9_III.explanation: Female teleworkers must have the same training, promotion, and participation opportunities as their on-site colleagues.
5_9_III.rationale: The invisibility of the teleworker can translate into exclusion from development opportunities; the standard requires equal access.
5_9_III.audit_criteria: Verify that the distribution of promotions, training, and strategic projects is equitable between on-site and remote teleworkers.

5_10.title: 5.10 — Privacy and Data Protection
5_10.obligation: The employer must respect the privacy of the teleworker in their home and ensure the protection of personal data and confidential company information during telework.
5_10.explanation: Implement information security policies for telework and respect the boundaries of the worker's home in supervision mechanisms.
5_10.rationale: Telework at the worker's home creates a tension between legitimate work supervision and the right to privacy in the home.
5_10.audit_criteria: Review information security policies for teleworkers and the supervision mechanisms implemented.

5_10_I.obligation: Respect the teleworker's right to privacy and intimacy in their home; supervision mechanisms must not violate that right.
5_10_I.explanation: Remote work monitoring tools must be limited to verifying work performance without invading the privacy of the domestic space.
5_10_I.rationale: Invasive supervision of the home violates fundamental rights of the worker and may constitute a discriminatory act.
5_10_I.audit_criteria: Review the supervision tools in use and confirm they are limited to work performance without access to private environments.

5_10_II.obligation: Implement information security measures to protect company and teleworker data during remote work.
5_10_II.explanation: Establish policies for using secure networks, handling confidential information, using VPN, and password management for telework.
5_10_II.rationale: Working from home or public networks exposes the company to IT security risks that must be proactively managed.
5_10_II.audit_criteria: Request the information security policy for teleworkers and the technical controls implemented.

5_11.title: 5.11 — Right to Disconnect
5_11.obligation: The employer must guarantee the teleworker's right to digital disconnection outside their working hours, on rest days, vacations, and leaves.
5_11.explanation: Establish a digital disconnection policy that prohibits requiring the teleworker's attention outside their ordinary working hours and during their rest periods.
5_11.rationale: The right to disconnect is a recognized labor right that protects the health and personal time of the worker.
5_11.audit_criteria: Verify the existence of the disconnection policy and the mechanisms to ensure its effective compliance.

5_12.title: 5.12 — Emergency and Accident Response
5_12.obligation: The employer must establish mechanisms to handle emergencies and accidents occurring during the telework workday, including incident communication and worker assistance.
5_12.explanation: Define the reporting and response protocol for occupational accidents in the telework modality, including communication channels with the employer.
5_12.rationale: Accidents occurring during the telework workday are occupational accidents; the employer has the same obligations as in on-site work.
5_12.audit_criteria: Request the emergency and accident response protocol for teleworkers and records of reported incidents.

5_13.title: 5.13 — Health and Social Security Services
5_13.obligation: The employer must ensure that teleworkers have the same social security coverage, health services, and benefits as on-site workers.
5_13.explanation: Teleworkers must be registered with the IMSS or the corresponding social security system under the same conditions as any other worker.
5_13.rationale: The telework modality does not modify the worker's social security rights; any difference constitutes a discriminatory act.
5_13.audit_criteria: Verify that teleworkers are registered with IMSS with correct salaries and have access to all legally required benefits.

5_14.title: 5.14 — Health Surveillance
5_14.obligation: The employer must conduct medical and health examinations for teleworkers based on the identified risk conditions, in order to detect and prevent health damage derived from the telework modality.
5_14.explanation: Include teleworkers in the company's medical surveillance program, with emphasis on telework-specific risks: musculoskeletal disorders, visual fatigue, and psychosocial risks.
5_14.rationale: Health surveillance enables early detection of health effects and allows preventive action; the teleworker has the same right to this service as the on-site worker.
5_14.audit_criteria: Request records of medical examinations conducted for teleworkers and verify that the surveillance program includes them.

5_8_a.description: Records of the identification and analysis of psychosocial risk factors: applied instruments, consolidated individual results, and analysis reports from each assessment cycle, retained for a minimum of 4 years.

5_8_b.description: Records of measures adopted to prevent and control psychosocial risk factors: action plans, implementation progress, modifications made, and results obtained, retained for a minimum of 4 years.

5_8_c.description: Records of medical examinations and psychological evaluations conducted on personnel exposed to psychosocial risk factors, retained under confidential custody for a minimum of 4 years.
